clue.text: Man covers page, two pages — it, symbolizes the country

indicators.note: one word covering another wraps around it, so the letters for man go outside the page

parts.note: a man is a male
a leaf of a book is a single sheet, giving two pages, front and back

explanation.surface: A man holds a document of a few pages that carries his nation's emblem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covers' puts P inside MALE to give MAPLE. The definition reads 'it symbolizes the country': Canada's flag carries the emblem.
explanation.definitionFit: The red leaf of the sugar tree is Canada's national emblem, shown on its flag.

clue.text: Army find a sort of native factotum.

indicators.note: a sort of something is a loose version of it, so these letters are reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: Soldiers come across a local servant who does every job going.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'a' after 'find' is part of the fodder (ARMYFINDA, nine letters), while 'a sort of' signals the rearrangement. The name comes from Robinson Crusoe's native companion and servant.
explanation.definitionFit: Defoe's islander became the byword for a loyal all-purpose assistant, a general dogsbody.

clue.text: Father finally celebrated after victory with flags

indicators.note: after places the closing letter of celebrated behind the victory letters

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
VE stands for Victory in Europe, as in VE Day

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word celebrated

explanation.surface: Dad rejoiced after the win, waving bunting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with flags' is not about bunting: flags are flagstones, so a path laid with flags has been surfaced with paving.
explanation.definitionFit: Flagstones are paving slabs, so ground laid with them has been surfaced in stone.

clue.text: Giant, in conclusion, set free

indicators.note: in places the word for giant within the word for conclusion

parts.note: a conclusion is an end
giant as an adjective means very large

explanation.surface: A giant is finally released.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set free' uses an old sense: to enlarge a prisoner was to release them, a usage still found in law and older literature.
explanation.definitionFit: In archaic and legal usage, to enlarge a captive meant to release them from confinement.

clue.text: English servant can set about a native

parts.note: a gyp is a college servant at Cambridge or Durham

indicators.note: set about means placed around, so the word for can goes around the a

parts.note: a tin is a can

explanation.surface: An English servant manages to tackle a local person.
explanation.walkthrough: A gyp is a college servant at Cambridge, a usage few outside Britain know. 'set about' signals one piece placed around the other, and the definition is simply 'native', a person born in a country.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone born and raised in Egypt is a native of that North African country.

clue.text: Punishment without it is limited

indicators.note: without in its older sense of outside means the punishment word wraps around it

parts.note: a fine is a monetary punishment

explanation.surface: A penalty that leaves something out is restricted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but here it carries its old meaning 'outside', so the punishment word goes around the other piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Something finite has bounds or an end, the opposite of infinite.

clue.text: Music for sportsmen

definitions.meaning: a melancholy style of music from the American South
at Oxford and Cambridge, sportsmen who have represented their university are awarded a Blue

explanation.definitionFit: The melancholy African-American music genre, and the Oxbridge sportsmen who have earned their university colours.

clue.text: Glass filled car component

definitions.meaning: a glass filled to the brim, as for a toast
the guard bar across the front or back of a car

explanation.definitionFit: A brimming glass of drink, and the shock-absorbing bar at each end of a vehicle.

clue.text: Eradicating and destroying group? Not I

indicators.note: destroying the arrangement of these letters breaks them up and rebuilds them into a new word

explanation.surface: Wiping out a gang, except me, of course.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is GROUP plus NOTI, nine letters; the question mark and 'Not I' make the surface a joke about excusing oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulling something out by the roots is wiping it out completely, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Recover, using remedy

definitions.meaning: an old sense meaning to save from loss, as goods from a wreck

explanation.definitionFit: To rescue goods from a wreck (as in salvage), and a healing ointment rubbed on a wound.

clue.text: Book terribly heartless but showing originality

parts.note: a novel is a book

indicators.note: heartless means the inside of the word terribly is removed, leaving its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A book that is dreadfully cruel but shows freshness of thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' looks like an adverb for 'heartless', but it is just the word to be gutted, leaving T and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Newness or freshness of an idea is what makes it original.

clue.text: For instance, one mule ran astray.

indicators.note: going astray means wandering off course, so these letters wander into a new order

explanation.surface: Here's an example: a mule bolted off.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the phrase 'For instance, one': the word 'one' is an example of a numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: A number word or figure such as one or 7 is a numeral, so 'one' is an instance.

clue.text: Employed in rather a daring detective agency

indicators.note: employed in means put to use within these words, so the letters sit inside the phrase rather a daring

explanation.surface: A firm of private investigators uses bold methods.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cheeky: the system that detects aircraft and ships is a detecting agent rather than a firm of investigators.
explanation.definitionFit: Echo-ranging by radio waves is the means by which aircraft and ships are detected.

clue.text: Leading article sandwiched between two vocal numbers

indicators.note: sandwiched between means the article is set as a filling between the two number words
vocal means the two number words are heard spoken rather than written

parts.note: the two numbers are two and four
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: The lead story is placed between two songs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading article' reads as a newspaper editorial, but 'Leading' is the definition. The two numbers, two and four, are heard rather than spelt, and 'sandwiched between' puts the article in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Being prominent or in front, ahead of the rest, is what leading means.

clue.text: In case, do exchange the bishop

indicators.note: exchange means swap the letters about so that they form a new word

explanation.surface: Just in case, swap the clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is INCASE plus DO, eight letters. The answer is used as a noun: a diocesan is the bishop in charge of a diocese.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop presiding over his own see is called its diocesan, a noun use of the adjective.

clue.text: Dislocated hip — tell me all the details at once

definitions.text: tell me all the details at once

parts.note: a dislocated joint is out, as in a shoulder put out
hip means fashionable, which is with it

explanation.surface: Someone with a damaged hip is urged to explain exactly what happened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hip' looks anatomical beside 'Dislocated', but it is the slang for fashionable, and 'Dislocated' means out of joint.
explanation.definitionFit: An impatient demand to say everything now, without delay or hedging.

clue.text: Musicians produce moving air.

definitions.meaning: the woodwind and brass players of an orchestra form its ... section
a current of air, a breeze

explanation.definitionFit: The orchestral section that blows into instruments, and air in motion such as a breeze.

clue.text: Refuse to believe the record Communist has it

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
a red is a communist

explanation.surface: Doubt the claim that a communist owns the album.
explanation.definitionFit: To reject something as untrue or unreliable is to doubt it.

clue.text: Crew member I beat in a race

parts.note: a hand is a member of a ship's crew
to cap is to outdo or top, so to beat

explanation.surface: A member of the crew says: I won the race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beat' reads as winning, but CAP means outdo. The definition 'a race' is a horse race where weights are set to even the field.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse race in which stronger runners carry more weight to give everyone an equal chance.

clue.text: Proof of foreign investment in show

indicators.note: investment in means being placed inside, as money is put into something, so the foreign word goes into the show word

parts.note: to evince is to show or display
de is the French for of

explanation.surface: Evidence of overseas money being put into a performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foreign investment' reads as overseas money, but 'of foreign' means the word 'of' in a foreign language (French), and 'investment in' places it inside the word for show.
explanation.definitionFit: Facts or signs that establish the truth of something serve as proof.

clue.text: Monster — once upon a time you rejected it

parts.note: ye is an old form of you

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the word it is read backwards

explanation.surface: A fairy-tale ogre, long ago, spurned something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once upon a time' signals an archaic word: YE, an old form of 'you'.
explanation.definitionFit: The abominable snowman, a legendary ape-like creature of the Himalayas.

clue.text: 8 possibly given something delightful in American city

indicators.note: possibly means the letters of that answer could also be arranged another way

parts.note: refers to the answer at 8 down, the word for a soothing remedy
a gas is informal for something great fun

explanation.surface: A remedy, perhaps, with a lovely treat in a US city.
explanation.walkthrough: '8' points to 8 down, SALVE; 'possibly' turns it into LASVE. A GAS is informal, especially American, for something great fun.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nevada gambling resort is a major US city.

clue.text: A doctor was first confused

parts.note: DD stands for Doctor of Divinity
to have led is to have been first

explanation.surface: A physician was the first to be muddled.
explanation.definitionFit: Muddled thinking is said to come from a brain gone off like a rotten egg.

clue.text: Composer of no great weight found in trading centre

indicators.note: found in means the light weight sits inside the market word

parts.note: a mart is a market
oz, an ounce, is a small weight

explanation.surface: A lightweight musician turns up at the market.
explanation.definitionFit: The Austrian prodigy who wrote The Magic Flute was a classical composer.

clue.text: Screen has double interference with vision

parts.note: a blind is a screen for a window
to fold is to double over

explanation.surface: A screen causes twice the obstruction to what one sees.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloth tied over the eyes stops someone seeing, an obstruction of sight.

clue.text: Brush — a sort of shrub

definitions.meaning: a yellow-flowered shrub of heaths and hillsides

explanation.definitionFit: A long-handled sweeping brush, and the yellow-flowered shrub whose twigs were once bound into such brushes.

clue.text: Furnishing with half a medal

indicators.note: half means only the front part of the medal word is taken

parts.note: a decoration is a medal

explanation.surface: Fitting out a room with part of a military honour.
explanation.walkthrough: DECORATION has ten letters; its first half gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The furnishings and ornament of a room make up its interior style.

clue.text: Vindicate conservative ruler

parts.note: Lear is Shakespeare's legendary king of Britain

explanation.surface: Exonerate the Tory leader.
explanation.walkthrough: LEAR is King Lear, the ruler in Shakespeare's tragedy.
explanation.definitionFit: To vindicate someone is to free them from blame or suspicion.

clue.text: Shakespearian character — work he took trouble returning

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word for trouble is read backwards

parts.note: to ail is to trouble

explanation.surface: A Shakespeare figure whose work went badly as he came back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns AIL into LIA. OPHELIA is Hamlet's ill-fated beloved.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet's beloved, who drowns, is one of the Bard's best-known heroines.

clue.text: Unfairly persuade nurse to take part in debate

parts.note: to con is to persuade by trickery
to tend is to nurse or care for

explanation.surface: Hoodwink a nurse into joining an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: To contend is to argue or dispute a point.

clue.text: Subdued letter from abroad to little boy

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet
Ted is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: A youngster is quietened by a letter from overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letter from abroad' sounds like foreign mail, but it is a foreign alphabet letter: Greek MU.
explanation.definitionFit: Muffled or toned down, made quieter, as in a subdued sound.

clue.text: Office — place about to be so strictly classified

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the whole run of letters for office and place is read backwards

parts.note: terce is a church office, the service of prayer at the third hour
a spot is a place

explanation.surface: A government building's location is to be kept under the highest security.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Office' is not a workplace but a church service, the prayers said at the third hour of the day. 'about' turns both pieces round together as one run of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest level of government security classification for documents.
